dataset_metadata.name: Data-driven capacity estimation of commercial lithium-ion batteries from voltage relaxation
dataset_metadata.institution: Tongji University, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT)
dataset_metadata.citation: Zhu, J. et al. Data-driven capacity estimation of commercial lithium-ion batteries from voltage relaxation. Nat. Commun. 13, 2261 (2022). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-29837-w
dataset_metadata.funding: Alexander von Humboldt Postdoctoral Research Program; National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC) Grant No. 52107230; NSFC Grant No. U20A20310; Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities; CELEST (Center for Electrochemical Energy Storage Ulm-Karlsruhe)

cell_info.cell_notes: Dataset 1. Cathode LiNi0.86Co0.11Al0.03O2, anode ~97 wt% C + ~2 wt% Si. Cutoff voltage 2.65-4.2 V. 1C = 3.5 A. 66 cells tested at 25/35/45 °C with charge rates 0.25C-1C and 1C discharge.
Dataset 2. Cathode LiNi0.83Co0.11Mn0.07O2, anode ~97 wt% C + ~2 wt% Si. Cutoff voltage 2.5-4.2 V. 1C = 3.5 A. 55 cells tested at 25/35/45 °C with charge rates 0.5C and 1C discharge.

Dataset 3. Cathode blend of 42(3) wt% Li(NiCoMn)O2 + 58(3) wt% Li(NiCoAl)O2, anode graphite. Cutoff voltage 2.5-4.2 V. 1C = 2.5 A. 9 cells tested at 25 °C with charge rate 0.5C and discharge rates 1C/2C/4C.

aging_modes.notes: Three sub-datasets: Dataset 1 (NCA, 66 cells), Dataset 2 (NCM, 55 cells), Dataset 3 (NCM+NCA, 9 cells). Discharge rate is constant at 1C for Datasets 1 and 2; for Dataset 3 it varies (1C, 2C, 4C). NCA and NCM cells tested 2016–2018; NCM+NCA cells tested in 2020.

time_protocol.notes: Relaxation rest after CV charge before discharge: 30 min for NCA and NCM batteries (real sampling time 120 s); 60 min for NCM+NCA battery (sampling time 30 s). Total cycles vary widely by condition: 50–800 (NCA), up to ~1500 (NCM), 750–850 (NCM+NCA).

rawdata.data_quality_notes: Each CSV has 9 columns: time/s, control/V/mA, Ecell/V, <I>/mA, Q charge/mAh, Q discharge/mAh, control/V, control/mA, cycle number.
rawdata.known_issues: Different experimenters at different test periods responsible for differences in battery connection methods and EIS experimental parameters (perturbation modes, amplitudes, OCV wait times) between NCA/NCM (2016–2018) and NCM+NCA (2020) cells.

checkup.notes: EIS measured at full charge (100% SOC). NCA cells: every 25 cycles, frequency 10 kHz–50 mHz, 20 points per decade, potential amplitude 20 mV, 30 min OCV rest before test. NCM cells: every 50 cycles, same frequency range and amplitude, 30 min OCV rest. NCM+NCA cells: every 50 cycles, frequency 10 kHz–0.01 Hz, 6 points per decade, sinusoidal amplitude 250 mA, 60 min OCV rest. Impedance raw data and fitting data available as separate Zenodo archive.

notes: The dataset contains cycling data for three types of commercial 18650 cells used to develop a data-driven capacity estimation approach based on voltage relaxation features after full charge. The Zenodo repository contains four zip files: Dataset_1_NCA_battery.zip (~553 MB), Dataset_2_NCM_battery.zip (~703 MB), Dataset_3_NCM_NCA_battery.zip (~340 MB), and Impedance raw data and fitting data.zip (~1.3 MB). Cells are labeled CYX-Y/Z where X=temperature, Y=charge C-rate, Z=discharge C-rate. 1C = 3.5 A for NCA and NCM cells; 1C = 2.5 A for NCM+NCA cells. The relaxation voltage curve after full charge is the primary feature source; six statistical features (Var, Ske, Max, Min, Mean, Kur) are extracted per cycle.
